# Release check-up

> Release check-up is QA for teams without a QA team: a pre-release testing tool for web apps. It scans a site, drafts a test plan, runs real-browser tests and writes a plain-language report with a ship / don't-ship verdict.

## What it checks
- Functionality: end-to-end user journeys run in a real browser (Playwright)
- Accessibility: contrast, labels, keyboard and structure problems
- Performance and security: load timing, headers, exposed secrets and risky patterns
- SEO: titles, meta descriptions, canonicals, headings, structured data, robots and sitemap
- AEO (answer engine optimization): question-style headings, FAQ/HowTo markup, concise answers
- GEO (generative engine optimization): entity clarity, llms.txt, AI-crawler access, citable facts

## How it works
1. Enter a site address and choose "only look" or full testing of your own test copy.
2. Review the scan and the drafted plan, then approve it.
3. Tests run; read the report, fix issues and re-run to confirm.

## Facts
- Free during the beta. A free shared online copy checks public sites, one check-up at a time; the same tool can be run on your own machine for private sites.
- On the shared online copy, AI keys and sign-ins are kept in memory for the visit only, and check-ups are visible to other people using that copy.
- AI features use only the API key the user supplies.
- "Only look" mode never fills in, sends or changes anything on the target site.
- Needs no hand-written tests.
